pages.quiz:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #8 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is the lesson of the hare and tortoise story? (1 mark)
   A. Tortoises are fast
   B. Never race
   C. Slow and steady wins the race
   D. Hares are lazy

2. A good storyteller (1 mark)
   A. forgets the ending
   B. practises and speaks clearly
   C. reads without looking
   D. whispers all the time

3. What is a reading club? (1 mark)
   A. A group that sells books
   B. A choir
   C. A team for running
   D. A group that meets to share and discuss books

4. What does Asiyesikia la mkuu huvunjika guu teach? (1 mark)
   A. Legs are weak
   B. Someone who ignores elders' advice may get hurt
   C. Never walk
   D. Elders are always wrong

5. Which is a proverb? (1 mark)
   A. Please sit down
   B. It is Monday
   C. A stitch in time saves nine
   D. Bring your book

6. What does A stitch in time saves nine mean? (1 mark)
   A. Sewing is easy
   B. Stitches are costly
   C. Nine is a lucky number
   D. Fix small problems early

7. What is a skit? (1 mark)
   A. A picture
   B. A short play
   C. A long poem
   D. A list

8. What is the language train game? (1 mark)
   A. Pupils build a story with sentences beginning with when
   B. A reading test
   C. A running race
   D. A game with real trains

9. What should you do if a stranger promises cheap goods and asks for money first? (1 mark)
   A. Be careful and ask an adult
   B. Send money at once
   C. Trust them
   D. Give your address

10. What is a vocabulary bank? (1 mark)
   A. A kind of poem
   B. A book cover
   C. A list of useful words on a theme
   D. A place for money

11. What should you check when you reorder jumbled words? (1 mark)
   A. That the sentence makes sense and has a verb
   B. The paper
   C. The colour of the letters
   D. Nothing

12. Which is a compound sentence? (1 mark)
   A. I bought a pen.
   B. The red pen.
   C. I saved money, so I bought a pen.
   D. A pen

13. What is the subject of a sentence? (1 mark)
   A. The full stop
   B. What is said about it
   C. The verb only
   D. Who or what the sentence is about

14. Which word shows a result? (1 mark)
   A. or
   B. so
   C. and
   D. but

15. Which is a domestic animal? (1 mark)
   A. Goat
   B. Zebra
   C. Lion
   D. Elephant

16. What does a preposition show? (1 mark)
   A. The position of one thing in relation to another
   B. The sound of an animal
   C. The price of goods
   D. The colour of a thing

17. What does intonation add to a poem? (1 mark)
   A. Extra pages
   B. The rise and fall of the voice that shows feeling
   C. A new title
   D. A picture

18. What does rhyme mean? (1 mark)
   A. Words with many letters
   B. Words with no vowels
   C. Words with capital letters
   D. Words with the same ending sound

19. What should you check in a partner's story? (1 mark)
   A. Title, characters, setting, problem and ending
   B. Only the pen
   C. Nothing
   D. Only the paper colour

20. Why should a writer plan a story before writing? (1 mark)
   A. To lose the ideas
   B. To organise the ideas
   C. To avoid a title
   D. To skip the ending

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain why pace matters when reading a poem. (3 marks)

22. Write a short story of five sentences that ends with the proverb A stitch in time saves nine. (5 marks)

23. Give three good manners to show when collecting proverbs from an elder. (3 marks)

24. Explain what the proverb Many hands make light work means. (2 marks)

25. Explain how the position game is played with objects on a table. (4 marks)

26. Give three tips for telling a story well. (3 marks)

27. Join the sentences with when: I counted my money. The bell rang. (2 marks)

28. Name two elements of a story. (2 marks)

29. What is a conjunction? Give one example. (2 marks)

30. Describe what an imaginative composition is. (2 marks)

31. Explain what the proverb Honesty is the best policy means. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES — TERMLY EXAM #8 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — Slow and steady wins the race
   The tortoise wins by steady effort.

2. B — practises and speaks clearly
   Practice and clarity make a good teller.

3. D — A group that meets to share and discuss books
   A reading club shares books and reading.

4. B — Someone who ignores elders' advice may get hurt
   It means one who does not listen to the elders may come to harm.

5. C — A stitch in time saves nine
   It is a short saying that gives advice.

6. D — Fix small problems early
   Early action prevents bigger trouble.

7. B — A short play
   A skit is a short acted scene.

8. A — Pupils build a story with sentences beginning with when
   Each pupil adds a when sentence.

9. A — Be careful and ask an adult
   Such offers may be tricks.

10. C — A list of useful words on a theme
   A word bank stores words to learn.

11. A — That the sentence makes sense and has a verb
   A sentence must make sense.

12. C — I saved money, so I bought a pen.
   It joins two sentences with so.

13. D — Who or what the sentence is about
   The subject is the topic of the sentence.

14. B — so
   So shows a result.

15. A — Goat
   Goats are kept by people.

16. A — The position of one thing in relation to another
   Prepositions show position such as on, under and beside.

17. B — The rise and fall of the voice that shows feeling
   Intonation shows meaning.

18. D — Words with the same ending sound
   Rhyming words sound alike at the end.

19. A — Title, characters, setting, problem and ending
   Peer review checks the elements.

20. B — To organise the ideas
   A plan gives the story shape.

SECTION B
----
21. (3 marks)
   Answer: A pace that is too fast makes words unclear, and one that is too slow loses interest. A good pace helps listeners follow and feel the mood.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of three ideas.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Any five clear sentences with a beginning, problem, ending and the proverb used correctly.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each sentence up to four and one mark for using the proverb correctly.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Greet politely, listen without interrupting, ask permission to write, say thank you.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: When people share a task, the work becomes easier and faster.
   Working / marking points: One mark for sharing work and one for easier work.

25. (4 marks)
   Answer: One pupil gives an instruction such as put the pencil on the book. Another follows it. The class checks whether the position is correct. Then the roles are swapped.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each of four points.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Start with a clear opening, tell events in order, speak clearly, look at the audience, end with what you learned.
   Working / marking points: One mark for each tip.

27. (2 marks)
   Answer: When I counted my money, the bell rang.
   Working / marking points: One mark for using when and one mark for the comma.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: Title, characters, setting, problem, events, ending (any two).
   Working / marking points: One mark for each.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: A conjunction is a joining word, such as and, but or when.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for an example.

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: A story that comes from the writer's imagination and is not a true report.
   Working / marking points: One mark for story and one for imagination.

31. (2 marks)
   Answer: Telling the truth is always the wisest choice because it builds trust.
   Working / marking points: One mark for the meaning and one for the reason.
